context.description: The status file is a projection of the machine snapshot

evidence.trustReason: Given the observed facts folded through the release-notes machine: the loaded plan's facts are folded with the real TaskEngineXState.initial/apply. When the status is projected: the real TaskStatus.project(plan, snapshot). Then each task, obligation and scenario carries its state, tags, blocked cause, start and end times and, for a task, its spans: every unit is compared with the snapshot's own selectors and context (present and absent keys too), and pinned to the facts: T1.1 trusted, start at task.started, end at task.verified, gapless spans waiting..trusted; T1.4 budget_exhausted with tags ended/stopped/dead, 3 attempts, 8 spans; T1.5 and T1 blocked by T1.4 with no start; T1.1.c1 trusted at its proof; blocked scenarios name a need in its projected state; S2 pending with no cause. And the run's title, spec id, path, start and end times and each scenario's loader title with no leading id: title equals the SPEC.md H1; spec, specId, path, startedAt = run.started; no endedAt while live, endedAt = the stop's at after a stop; each title equals its acceptance 'Scenario:' line without the id. And no state of its own, no phase or dependency tags: after every fold prefix only class tags in AD-1 order while the snapshot holds phase and waits: tags; every state equals the engine view; waitingOn equals the machine's waits selector; a plan with emptied dependency lists projects the same. And the old derivations no longer exist: no runState/waitingOn/trusted/ACTIVE/Input export or declaration in status.ts, no read of after/afterEffective/needs/supports, and the only such function in src/task is the engine's waits selector. And an obligation carries no blocked cause: no blockedBy key and no blocked tag on any obligation after any prefix, while blocked tasks and scenarios have causes. Fresh run: 5 pass, 0 fail, 4394 expect calls.
